brief: For Hungary's foreign-owned banks the analytical layer genuinely sits at the parent: KBC (K&H, inside the International Markets business unit), Erste Group (Hungary as a named geographic segment), RBI (Hungary as a Central Europe country segment, with unusually explicit clearing/settlement/payment commission commentary) and UniCredit (Hungary inside the CEE division perimeter) each publish English-language quarterly reports and presentations on a fixed calendar, plus Intesa Sanpaolo's quarterly press releases covering CIB Bank within its International Subsidiary Banks Division. Two of the six named actors do not hold: Magyar Cetelem passed from BNP Paribas Personal Finance to Cofidis / Credit Mutuel Alliance Federale in October 2024, and no Hungarian entity surfaced in Santander Consumer Finance's disclosed geographies — both should be re-scoped rather than monitored as-is. No parent publishes in Hungarian, so local-language coverage in this cell comes from the subsidiaries' own statutory report pages (kh.hu, raiffeisen.hu) and from Portfolio.hu / Privatbankar.hu, which convert the Vienna and Brussels releases into HUF-denominated Hungary-only stories within hours. Practical collection risk is link stability rather than access: KBC and RBI serve result PDFs from CDN paths carrying rotating cache tokens, so assets must be resolved from IR index pages at collection time instead of templated.
